title: Catheter care at home
what: How to care for a bladder catheter and urine bag at home to prevent infection.
why: When a catheter has been placed for a while or long term, and you are going home.
duration: care takes a few minutes a day; your doctor will say when to change the catheter
tell_doctor: When the catheter was placed and when it needs changing
If you are allergic to latex
If care is hard for you, and you need a nurse's help

prepare.title: What to buy
prepare.text: Spare urine bags, a larger night bag, soap, and clean towels. Check the list with the nurse.

prepare.title: Training
prepare.text: Before going home, ask the nurse to show you how to change and empty the bag.

prepare.title: Contacts
prepare.text: Write down who to call if the catheter stops working.

bring: Your discharge papers with the date the catheter was placed
The clinic's or nurse's phone number
steps: Wash your hands with soap before any care
Once or twice a day, wash the skin around the catheter with warm soapy water
Keep the bag below the level of your bladder
Empty the bag when it is half to two thirds full
Make sure the tube is not kinked
Change the bag when the nurse told you to
feel: Sometimes an urge to pee. This is normal
A little leaking around the catheter can happen
after: Drink enough water, unless your doctor has limited it
A nurse or doctor changes the catheter. Do not pull it out yourself
Showers are usually fine. Ask your doctor about baths and pools
red_flags: No urine flows into the bag for a few hours, and your belly swells and hurts
Urine is cloudy, smells bad, or has blood
The catheter falls out: do not put it back yourself. Call your doctor

faq.q: Can I go out and work with a catheter?
faq.a: Yes. The bag straps to your leg under your clothes. Just keep it below your bladder.

faq.q: Why does urine leak around the catheter?
faq.a: It can happen with bladder spasms or a kinked tube. Check the tube. If it does not stop, tell your doctor.

reminders.text: Bag or catheter change is planned for tomorrow. Check that you have a spare bag.
